A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EVSSM for image deblurring, with matching architecture, benchmarks, and sections. Their complete text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original EVSSM results for deblurring, deraining, and dehazing, along with scanning and geometric-transformation ablations and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: V2 reports original EVSSM benchmark results and component ablations, including a newly reported DFFN-versus-EDFFN efficiency experiment.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a 1D depth-wise convolution after the projections generating the selective-scan parameters B, C, and delta (Section 3.2, Equation 5). This is a localized modification to EVS. The encoder-decoder, geometric transformations, loss, and EDFFN's placement of frequency filtering at the FFN output already exist in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate deblurring on GoPro, HIDE, and RealBlur-J/R, deraining on the same real-world rain dataset, and dehazing on RESIDE-6K. V2's replacement of RealBlur scene counts with image counts does not establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes across several experiments. V2 adds MLWNet-B on GoPro/HIDE and MLWNet on RealBlur; adds GoPro entries for SAPHN, DeepRFT+, and MPRNet-local and HIDE entries for DeepRFT+ and CU-mamba. MAXIM disappears from the GoPro table despite remaining in the prose. DSC and DCP are removed from deraining and dehazing comparisons, and Table 8 drops DMPHN and MPRNet-local. MLWNet also replaces FFTformer in Figure 2 and DeblurGAN-v2 in Figure 3.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported optimizer from ADAM to AdamW. The new EDFFN experiment introduces FFN-only comparison models and GPU-memory measurement. The main progressive-training stages, patch and batch sizes, PSNR/SSIM metrics, and GoPro-to-HIDE evaluation procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted DFFN-versus-EDFFN ablation measuring reconstruction quality, parameters, GPU memory, and runtime (Table 7). It removes the qualitative scanning and geometric-transformation examples in v1 Figures 4–5, while retaining their corresponding quantitative ablation studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Runtime averages remain point estimates; the added GPU-memory measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results change across all retained tasks: EVSSM PSNR changes from 34.50 to 34.51 on GoPro, 31.97 to 31.99 on HIDE, 34.15/41.04 to 34.34/41.27 on RealBlur-J/R, 48.78 to 49.00 for deraining, and 31.66 to 32.05 for dehazing. The scanning ablation changes more substantially: two-/four-direction PSNR falls from 34.08/34.05 to 33.08/33.05, reversing their ranking relative to one-direction scanning. Retained baseline values also change, including Restormer's HIDE scores. New Table 7 reports DFFN/EDFFN runtimes of 75/36 ms. These are revised or additional results, not controlled gains under an unchanged method and optimizer.

T1.justification: Equation 5 substantively revises the mathematical definition of scan-parameter generation to include DConv1D(Linear(X1)) and explicitly passes the resulting parameters into S6. The loss, continuous and discretized state-space equations, and geometric-transformation rule remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 promotes the existing EDFFN component into the abstract and explicit contributions. It also claims quarter computational cost relative to existing SSM methods, broadening v1's discussion of fourfold differences specifically in scanning cost. The central deblurring objective and favorable-performance conclusion remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds a mechanism argument that linear-only parameter projections limit spatial diversity and that 1D convolutions combined with geometric transformations capture richer multidirectional context. It further explains EDFFN efficiency through reduced channel counts during frequency processing. The stated limitation to simple flip/transpose transformations and proposed future polar transformations is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies a 300K-iteration ablation schedule with cosine decay from 0.001 to 0.000001 and gives RealBlur image counts instead of scene counts. These disclosures do not establish changed splits or an increased training budget. The new convolution's kernel is inconsistently described as size 7 in Section 3.2 and 1×1 after Equation 5. Hardware information and the code-link destination remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the MLWNet and LinGen papers, removes the GAN discussion and several high-level vision references, and drops references associated with DSC, DCP, and Adam. Its central positioning against costly multi-direction scanning and FFTformer's frequency-domain FFN remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and portions of the introduction and related work, presents contributions as bullets, and expands the method explanations. It also adds an author and acknowledgments and revises affiliations. These are localized edits within the retained six-section organization; substantial portions of the narrative and conclusion remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, including an expanded selective-scan parameter pathway. GoPro and HIDE results are merged into one table, other tables are restructured, an EDFFN table is added, and two qualitative ablation figures are removed. Figures 2–3 also replace comparator panels.

improvement.justification: The EDFFN ablation and MLWNet comparisons strengthen empirical support, but v2 introduces unresolved problems affecting central evidence and reproducibility. Table 5 reverses the scanning-baseline PSNR ranking without reconciling the discussion, and the new convolution has conflicting kernel specifications. Section 4.2 also swaps the RealBlur-J/R improvement margins, while the broader quarter-cost claim is not established by the complexity comparisons. These benefits and weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
